name: veterinary_clinic_system_069_transfer_chain_consistency
instruction:
The location transfer log must be consistent with current patient locations. For each patient with one or more completed transfers, only the latest completed transfer (ordered by requested_at, then id as tie-breaker) should reflect the patient's current location. Any earlier completed transfer for that patient whose to_location_id does not match the patient's current location_id is a stale record and must be marked status='superseded' and chain_fixed='<batch_code>'. Do not modify patients, pending transfers, or approved transfers - only completed transfer rows.

Then:
1. Push one ops_reports row per patient with completed transfers report='transfer_chain', batch_code, patient_id, chain_length, superseded_count, current_location_matches (true if the latest completed transfer's to_location_id equals the patient's current location_id).
2. Push one ops_reports summary row report='transfer_chain_summary', batch_code, total_patients_with_completed, total_superseded, total_pending, total_approved.
3. For each superseded transfer, push one communications row to the owner: channel='email', direction='outbound', subject 'Transfer record superseded for <patient.name> - <batch_code>', body 'Location transfer <transfer_id> for <patient.name> has been marked superseded because a later completed transfer reflects the patient's current location.', logged_by='system', occurred_at episode, owner_id and patient_id set.
4. Push one audit_log row: action='TRANSFER_CHAIN_RECONCILED', actor='system', actor_role='system', target_collection='location_transfers', target_id='batch', details='Batch <batch_code> - <N> superseded transfers', occurred_at episode.

All changes keyed by the live batch code so a re-run reaches the same end state.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Completed transfer chains are reconciled: earlier completed transfers with to_location_id != patient current location are status='superseded' with chain_fixed=batch. Latest completed transfers and non-completed transfers are unchanged. ops_reports has one transfer_chain row per patient with completed transfers and one transfer_chain_summary. communications has one row per superseded transfer owner. audit_log has the batch entry.

checks.expect: exact superseded set and unchanged latest/non-completed transfers
superseded set and chain counts computed two independent ways (Python vs SQL)

hazards: Patient 26 (Barnaby, owner 22) has two completed transfers: id 5 (requested 2026-06-06, to_location_id 1) and id 6 (requested 2026-08-20, to_location_id 3). Patient 26's current location_id is 3. The later transfer (id 6) matches; the earlier (id 5) must be superseded. A solution that uses the first completed transfer or does not compare to current location will fail.

Patient 15 (Truffle) has one completed transfer id 3 (requested 2026-08-05, to_location_id 3) and current location_id 3. No supersede. A solution that marks all completed transfers except the latest as superseded regardless of to_location_id would incorrectly supersede id 3.

Patients 3, 10, and 30 have pending transfers (ids 1, 2, 7) to locations different from their current locations. Patient 19 has an approved transfer id 4 (to_location_id 2) and current location_id 2. Pending and approved transfers must not be modified; only completed rows are adjusted.

A solution that 'fixes' the problem by changing the patient's location_id to match the latest transfer, or by changing an approved/pending transfer to completed, would violate the 'fix the transfer rows only' rule.
The superseded set is determined by requested_at ordering, not by transfer id order. The later completed transfer by date is the authority; id order is only the tie-breaker.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Combines temporal chain reasoning (latest completed transfer wins) with per-patient and summary ops_reports, owner communications, and audit log, plus dual-path verification of the superseded set, while strictly not modifying patients or non-completed transfers.
